newsitem.title: USA: Mental health coverage not as costly as thought.
newsitem.headline: Mental health coverage not as costly as thought.

text.p: Treating mental illnesses like physical ones may be much more affordable than previously thought and not lead to skyrocketing insurance costs, a new government study said Tuesday.
A law enacted last year will require insurance plans that cover severe mental illnesses to treat those illnesses the same way as they treat other ailments starting next January.

The findings by the National Advisory Mental Health Council directly contradict previous studies and insurance industry warnings that indicated expanding mental health benefits would send premiums soaring.
It showed that caring for the mentally ill is more affordable than believed, if done through a managed care plan. Earlier studies were not based on a managed care model.
"This report is good news. It clearly shows that parity for mental illness is affordable," said Sen. Pete Domenici, a New Mexico Republican who was a key sponsor of mental health parity.

"Although preliminary, this and other findings do not support earlier concerns about potentially high financial costs caused by parity," said Dr. Darrel Regier, director of health policy research at the National Institute of Mental Health.

The parity law is not as sweeping as some advocates for the mentally ill wished, but it was a step toward covering such illnesses the same way as physically debilitating ailments. Regier said further studies would monitor the quality of mental health services under the parity rule.
